summary: Ryojin Soga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Otani University, Shinshu University, Kōkōdō, and under Manshi Kiyozawa. He served as a professor at Toyo University and Otani University, where he also became the 17th president.

Ryojun Mitomo is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held a professorship at Rissho University Junior College (attested 1996) and served as a professor in the Faculty of Social Welfare at Rissho University (attested 2001).
Ryokei Kaginushi was a Buddhist studies scholar. His career included posts at Otani University as a professor in the Faculty of Letters (attested 1978) and as professor (attested 1993).
Ryoken Nawa works in indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a commissioned researcher at Kyoto Koka Women's University (attested 2015) and as a lecturer at Osaka University (attested 2026).

Ryoko Mochizuki is a scholar of indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo between approximately 1957 and 1963. Mochizuki served as a lecturer at Rissho University, attested in 1972 and 1983.

Ryosaburo Sakaki studied at the Third Higher School and the University of Tokyo, working in indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He lectured at Ryukoku University (1897) and held professorships at the Third Higher School (1899) and Kyoto University (1908).

Ryosei Fukuda, a Buddhist studies scholar, completed his studies and doctorate at Toyo University. He was a professor (from 1973) and professor emeritus (2007) at Taisho University, and later served as visiting professor at Shuchiin University (2012).

Ryoshin Nakao is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. Nakao served as a staff member at the Soto-shu Shumu Kenkyujo and as a professor (attested 1998) and professor emeritus (attested 2026) at Hanazono University.

Ryosho Hayashi worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology after studying at Taisho University and Tokyo Metropolitan University. At Taisho University, Hayashi became a professor in 1975, dean of the Faculty of Letters in 1981, and professor emeritus (1990–1994).

Ryosho Nakamura studied indology and philosophy at Seventh Higher School Zoshikan, Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, and Rissho University. He served as a professor at The International University of Kagoshima from around 1965 to 1998.

Ryosho Tanaka studied at Komazawa University, working in Buddhist studies and sinology. He served Komazawa University as assistant, professor, dean, museum director, and president, and also held a professorship at Ryukoku University.

Ryoshu Koda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and indology who studied under Seitatsu Matsunami. Koda held researcher posts at Taisho University (attested 1998) and the Hasegawa Institute for Buddhist Culture (attested 2006).

Ryoshu Michihata was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at Otani University (~1925–1928). Michihata later held posts at Otani University (~1946–1965) and served as a professor at Kyoto Koka Women's University (~1965–1980).
Ryoshu Misaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University from around 1947 to 1952. Misaki later served as a professor emeritus at Waseda University (attested 1988–2000).

Ryoshun Okubo studied at Waseda University, specializing in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Okubo became Professor of Sino-Japanese Buddhism at Waseda University (~2000) and held posts at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Ryudo Fujii is a scholar of indology and philosophy who studied under Albrecht Wezler and Harunaga Isaacson. Fujii held posts at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (2003), Kokushikan University (2010), and Kyoto Women's University (2015).

Ryugen Tanemura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and indology. Posts include part-time lecturer at Nishogakusha University (attested 2013), researcher at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2014), and faculty member at Taisho University (attested 2014–2026).

Ryuhiko Taga is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University. He spent his academic career at Rissho University as a lecturer, associate professor, professor (~1975–2001), and president (~1992–1998).

Ryuichi Abe studied at Keio, Johns Hopkins, Taisho, and Columbia under several scholars. Active in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies, he was Kao Associate Professor at Columbia (1998–2004) before becoming Reischauer Institute Professor at Harvard around 2003.

Ryuji Hayashi, a scholar of Buddhist studies and indology, studied at the University of Delhi. Hayashi held academic posts at Tohoku University, Sendai National College of Technology, Kodomo Education Hosen University, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
